intro: Close to the mound of Troy, in Çanakkale province, stands the Troy Museum, opened in 2018. Notice its shape: a cube half-sunk into the ground. Inside, it lays out Troy's nine layers and traces what was carried away from the city.
history: The museum opened in 2018, about a kilometre from the mound. It was designed as a rusted steel cube sunk into the ground, so that the building, like the excavation, is read from the bottom up. The display works through Troy's nine layers in order, and it states plainly where the objects taken from the city — the Treasure of Priam among them — are held today.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the nine layers and the Polyxena Sarcophagus, then the gold jewellery, and finally the history of the excavations.
facts: Did you know? The 'Treasure of Priam' that Schliemann removed went first to Germany, vanished in the Second World War, and surfaced in Moscow in 1993. It is still in Russia today. And the museum itself was designed as a rusted steel cube sunk into the ground, so you walk it from the bottom up, just like the excavation.
outro: This brings our journey through the Troy Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These objects have travelled a long road through time; let them rest here safely for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
